ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

3. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

5. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

6. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

8. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. goed

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

10. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

12. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Where is the library?

2. B — run

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

8. A — went

9. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
